explanations: The dedup key is built from workspace, file, kind and content hash, but not from version or eventId. If a user edits a file A -> B -> A within the 10-minute window, the third change (a new, higher version) gets the same key as the first one. It is dropped as a duplicate before applyIfNewer runs, so the index stays on B and other devices never sync the revert. The key should identify the delivery (eventId), or at least include the version.

The upsert only updates when `file_index.version < EXCLUDED.version`. If the stored version is the same, rowCount is 0, so the processor logs "stale change ignored", remembers the event and returns without calling fanOut. ON CONFLICT handles the key clash, so nothing throws. A rollback cannot happen because older or equal versions never overwrite the row.

JavaScript Maps iterate in insertion order, and set() on an existing key keeps its original position. Deleting first moves the refreshed key to the end. Both evictExpired (which stops at the first unexpired entry) and the maxEntries trim (which removes keys().next()) assume the first keys are the oldest. Map.set does not throw on existing keys, and memory is not the reason.

ChangeDeduplicator is an in-memory Map, so a restart starts it empty. Redelivered events then reach applyIfNewer, whose version guard turns repeats into no-ops with no fan-out. Nothing reloads the Map from Postgres, and replicas do not share it. Because of the version check, the in-memory dedup is an optimization rather than the only safeguard.
